title: releasing the savings hold (account 1) restores available to 1000.31 while the posted balance stays 1000.31
_note: Parity vector transcribed from the post-release account read-back, capture savings-hold-release/out/savings-hold-after-release-account-raw.json (GET /savingsaccounts/1?associations=all, tenant gerege, HTTP 200). The stream is the post-hold stream plus the AMOUNT_RELEASE row id 7 (transactionType.id 21, amountRelease true, amount 137.290000, runningBalance 1000.310000) and the hold row id 6 now carrying releaseTransactionId 7 (= release_id_of_hold_amount 7). expect.account_balance_minor is summary.accountBalance 1000.31 = 100031, still unmoved; expect.held_minor is 0 because the hold id 6 is discharged by id 7 and HeldOf pairs them by identity, not arithmetic; expect.available_minor is summary.availableBalance 1000.31 = 100031, restored. This vector completes the rule with the fourth limb: release restores available and the balance still has not moved. The after-hold vector (SV-07) carries the limb a release-only port cannot see, so both states are promoted.

provenance.note: The expected cells are transcribed from the committed post-release account read-back; that one document carries both the summary (accountBalance, availableBalance) and the transaction list, so held, balance and available are all read from a single observed state. capture_case_id is the account number the rows belong to.
provenance.citation: savings-hold-after-release-account-raw.json account id 1 (accountNo 000000001), summary {"accountBalance":1000.31,"availableBalance":1000.31}, transaction id 6 (AMOUNT_HOLD) {"amount":137.29,"releaseTransactionId":7}, transaction id 7 (AMOUNT_RELEASE, transactionType.id 21) {"amount":137.29,"amountRelease":true,"runningBalance":1000.31}; the three pre-hold rows are transaction id 1 (DEPOSIT) {"amount":1000.0}, id 3 (INTEREST_POSTING) {"amount":0.15} and id 2 (INTEREST_POSTING) {"amount":0.16}
